'''Osvaldo Alfredo Reig''' (14 August 1929 – 13 March 1992) was an [[Argentina|Argentine]] [[biologist]] and [[paleontology|paleontologist]]. He was born in [[Buenos Aires]], Argentina.

He made numerous contributions in the fields of [[paleontology]] and biological [[evolution]]. He studied at the [[Universidad de La Plata]], but did not complete his studies. Later he worked at the [[University of Buenos Aires]] in the Department of Biological Sciences working with the biological evolution of mammals. In 1966 he began work at the [[Museum of Comparative Zoology]] at [[Harvard University]]. He worked for almost fifteen years at the [[Central University of Venezuela]] and the [[Simón Bolívar University (Venezuela)|Simón Bolívar University]]. In 1973 he received his PhD in Zoology and Paleontology from the [[University of London]].<ref name="Roig 1992"/> Among the important papers he authored was the description of ''[[Herrerasaurus]]'', one of the earliest [[dinosaur]]s known.  

In 1955, Reig was a founding member of the Asociación Paleontológica Argentina alongside [[Mathilde Dolgopol de Sáez]]. 

Reig died in 1992.
